item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q017_prp8_evolutionary_mosaic","answer":"SCOPe decomposes Prp8 in PDB 3jb9 into five domains: an N-terminal Prp8-specific domain, a reverse-transcriptase-like domain, a type-II restriction-endonuclease-like domain, an RNase-H-like domain, and a C-terminal Jab1/MPN domain. The latter four connect Prp8 structurally to previously characterized mobile-element or enzyme modules—especially the reverse-transcriptase and nuclease machinery associated with group II introns—whereas the N-terminal domain represents a newly observed fold. Thus Prp8 is an evolutionary mosaic, consistent with spliceosomal ancestry involving group II intron-related components plus a later Prp8-specific structural addition. These relationships must be interpreted at their SCOPe level: a shared superfamily supports probable ancestry, while fold-level resemblance alone does not prove homology. Nor should nuclease, reverse-transcriptase, RNase H, or JAMM-metalloprotease activity be transferred automatically to Prp8; several modules are highly diverged and function principally as spliceosomal scaffolds or interaction surfaces. Templates should therefore be selected domain by domain rather than treating full-length Prp8 as homologous to any one of these proteins.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
